text:
Sam Chen: Heads up — our ap-southeast1 canary pool started failing node boots after the nvidia-driver 551 rollout a few minutes ago. DKMS compile errors across cos-node images.
Priya Rao: Noted, seeing same symptom in one us-west1 canary too. Jobs hitting GPU queue backlog.
Jorge Alvarez: Quick log dump from a failing node:
```
DKMS: build started for nvidia-551/1.0 for kernel 5.15.0-1030-gke
make: Entering directory '/var/lib/dkms/nvidia-551/1.0/build'
make[1]: *** No rule to make target '/lib/modules/5.15.0-1030-gke/build', needed by 'modules'.  Stop.
ERROR: Cannot find the kernel headers for kernel 5.15.0-1030-gke.
modprobe: FATAL: Module nvidia_uvm not found in directory /lib/modules/5.15.0-1030-gke
```
Linh Tran: That looks like kernel-headers mismatch after autoupdate on some nodes. Cos images in ap-southeast still on 5.15, but our node image build used 5.19 for the driver package.
Maya Patel: infra-bot shows rollout started at 2103456700 by @deploy-team with batch size 5. Can we pause? @infra-bot can you halt the staged rollout and tag the canaries? :pray:
infra-bot: Rollout pause requested. Cancelling remaining batches. All canary nodes marked for investigation.
Sam Chen: Good. For immediate mitigation: 1) mark affected nodes unschedulable, 2) drain and reprovision with pinned driver 550 image, 3) notify customer-facing queues about potential delays.
Priya Rao: I'm seeing NCCL warnings on some rebuilt nodes too — possibly ABI mismatch when kernel modules didn't load cleanly. Example: `NCCL WARN Call to ibv_create_cq failed` after driver reload.
Jorge Alvarez: Repro steps I used: provision a new cos-node from template, install nvidia-driver-551 .deb, run `dkms install nvidia/551 -k $(uname -r)` -> fails with headers error. Works if I install linux-headers-$(uname -r) first, but GKE managed nodes don't always have headers package available.
Linh Tran: That's the crux — our managed node images don't guarantee headers on disk. Driver .deb assumes headers or a running kernel-devel. DKMS path is brittle for these kernels.
Maya Patel: Ops ask: how many GPUs are impacted and what's the cost hit if we shift traffic to other regions?
Sam Chen: Early estimate: ~120 GPUs in ap-southeast and ~40 in us-west impacted. If we burst to other regions using on-demand, rough cost delta ~+18% for this weekend.
Priya Rao: Short-term plan: rollback to 550 across canaries, block 551 from reaching remaining fleets, and draft a runbook to build node images with kernel-headers or use precompiled kernel modules.
Jorge Alvarez: I'll prepare a rollback patch to the deployment job and a verifiable smoke test that checks `/lib/modules/$(uname -r)/nvidia.ko` presence and `nvidia-smi` output before marking node ready.
Linh Tran: Also suggest adding a DKMS-free packaging path: ship vendor kernel modules built for our common kernel versions to avoid on-node compiles. Cuts risk.
Maya Patel: I'll open an incident page and notify support. Tagging @oncall for next shift handover.
Sam Chen: Thanks — +1 on the vendor-modules approach. After rollback we'll schedule a controlled re-test against a pinned image with headers present, then gradually re-roll with smaller batches.
Priya Rao: Filing ticket with GKE node-image team to confirm why headers vanished on some pools.
infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-214 — "Driver 551 DKMS failures / node boot". Assigned to eng-infra.
Sam Chen: Okay locking this thread. Keep updates in the incident doc. :thumbsup:
